newsItems.headline: Gold recovers from two-week low ahead of US inflation - Reuters
UK's FTSE 100 flat as energy gains counter mining losses amid US-Iran flare-up - Reuters

riskTone.label: NEUTRAL
riskTone.rationale: US-Iran flare-up adds mild risk-off pressure; gold recovery and flat FTSE suggest contained anxiety, no strong directional signal.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture: GBP/USD is up +0.46% today, sitting at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range — meaning sterling is unusually strong right now. Because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes FTSE's dollar-earning giants like Shell, HSBC and Unilever worth less in sterling terms), this is a headwind for the index, and the snapshot flags it as a BEARISH drag. Despite that, the broader picture tilts bullish: Brent crude is up a striking +4.41%, which is directly positive for Shell and BP — the energy sector is flagged BULLISH and these are top-5 index weights. Copper is up +1.89%, lifting the miners (Rio, Glencore, Anglo) — also BULLISH. US futures are modestly positive (S&P 500 +0.36%), and the VIX [a measure of expected US market volatility] sits at 17.5, a NORMAL regime that doesn't dampen risk appetite. UK gilts [government bonds] have edged slightly lower in yield (-2bp on the 10-year), with no long-end stress signal, so there's no fiscal alarm ringing today. The most relevant recent headline (Reuters, ~21 hours ago) cited a US-Iran flare-up as the likely driver behind oil's surge — geo-political tension lifted Brent and kept FTSE roughly flat as energy gains offset mining weakness earlier; that dynamic has since shifted more constructively. No fresh market-moving headlines in the last few hours. The overall directional bias is BULLISH (score +4/10), with the oil and copper commodity complex doing most of the heavy lifting, but the strong GBP acts as a meaningful offset, keeping the index up only +0.11% on the day. Confidence is 5/10 — the big wildcard is US CPI [Consumer Price Inflation — a key measure of how fast prices are rising], which prints at 13:30 BST today and is HIGH impact; a hot reading could spike the dollar, push GBP lower (which would actually help FTSE via the sign-flip), but could also spook US equity futures and drag UK100 down with them — the net effect is genuinely uncertain. On the ORB [Opening Range Breakout — a trade that buys or sells when price moves outside the first 30-minute price range after market open]: the range broke DOWNWARD at the open, which means a short trade was triggered, but with 72% of the 14-day average daily range [the typical daily price swing, averaged over two weeks — ADR14 is 128.1 points] already consumed by 13:11 BST, there is limited room left for further downside extension; any ORB short taken at the open would now be approaching its natural range limit, making new entries unattractive. The ORB high sits at 10,488 and low at 10,447, with price currently at 10,502 — notably, price has already reclaimed above the ORB high, suggesting the initial downside break may have been a fakeout (a false move that quickly reverses). Today looks more like a fakeout/sweep-then-reverse day than a clean trend day, and the 13:30 CPI print makes it a stand-aside environment for new ORB entries. For scheduled events: US CPI is at 13:30 BST today — treat the 30 minutes either side as a no-trade zone. Looking ahead, UK GDP Monthly Estimate prints at 07:00 BST on Wednesday (16 July), a HIGH-impact release that will set the tone for Wednesday's open and could reset the week's directional bias entirely — prepare for potential overnight gaps heading into that session. Key levels: overnight high 10,499.9 and overnight low 10,414.8 define the broader range; ORB high 10,488 is now acting as support after the reclaim; prior day high 10,526.3 is the next upside target; with 72% of ADR used, expect slowing momentum and possible mean-reversion into the close. The single thing to remember today: energy and copper are doing the heavy lifting for the bulls, but with CPI in 20 minutes and 72% of the daily range already spent, this is a day to watch, not chase.
